title: Gaming: smaller batches for the chart’s sake, and other honest-looking lies

videos.script: Here are the Billing team's numbers for August and September. Four and a half deployments a week, and five per cent of them failing. {{numbers}} Now watch them improve. {{watch}} Count each change as its own deployment, and the frequency nearly doubles. The failure rate drops to three per cent. {{split}} Decide that a failure only counts if it took more than an hour to fix, and the failure rate becomes zero. {{redefine}} Nothing happened to the code. Nothing happened to the users. Nobody lied, either. {{nothing}} Each step can be defended in a meeting. That is what makes gaming dangerous. {{defend}} This lesson performs the tricks on purpose, so you can recognise them. Then it shows the signatures they leave behind. {{signatures}} And it ends where the defence really is: making the trick pointless. {{pointless}}
